answer: Each identity must anchor to one power meter. The forge book gives one paper per meter, and the harbor book lists each meter once, so one meter backs one identity. The identity locks a 90 credit bond. Harbor checkers match its plume, its pattern, to the hours it claims; a mismatch burns the bond. The k-th meter pays 20 plus 35 per prior meter, so the k-th fake costs 110 plus 35 times k minus 1; 1,000 fakes cost 17,592,500 credits. A rented meter farm fails: a rented plume tracks its owner's hours, not the renter's work. One honest agent pays one 90 bond, back after a clean epoch.
